To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

susceptibility to both persistent epidermal proliferation and skin tumorigenesis following a single high dose of UV radiation is inherited as a recessive trait in F1 hybrids derived from crosses between SENCAR hypersusceptible and C57BL6 or BALB/c resistant parental strains.

(1) susceptibility to both photomutogenesis and persistent hyperplastic epidermis is inherited in a similar, recessive manner; (2) susceptibility to both traits can be expressed in the F1 hybrids between the susceptible and resistant strains, but at a lower incidence than in the susceptible strain; and (3) the results are consistent with a model in which the two characteristics are causally related, rather than two distinct phenotypes.

susceptibility to phototumor formation in mice is a polygenic trait that is controlled by at least two genes, one of which is dominant to the SENCAR genotype, and one of which is recessive to the SENCCAR genotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and molecular basis for the development of skin cancer and persistent hyperplastic lesions following UV radiation exposure in SENCAR mice.
the identification and characterization of the genetic basis of susceptibility to UV radiation-induced skin cancer.

the identification and characterization of genes that control the response to environmental carcinogens, and the present studies have demonstrated that susceptibility to both photomutagenesis and persistent hyper-plasia is controlled by a single locus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SENCAR mouse is a unique model for persistent hyperplasia because of its hypersusceptibility, and that susceptibility to both photodermatosis (hyperplasia and tumours) is inherited as a single trait.
susceptibility to phototumor induction is completely recessive in F1 hybrids of SENCAR x C57BL/ 6 mice, and is only partially recessive in SENCAR x BALB/c mice.

susceptibility to phototurnorigenesis and to persistent hyperplasia are inherited as incompletely recessive traits in the F1 crosses between SENCAR (Hs) and BALB/c (hs) mice, but are completely recessive in the SENCAR (HS) X C57BL/ 6 (HS) cross.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
susceptibility to persistent hyperplasia is completely recessive and is controlled by a single gene.
the susceptibility to phototumor formation and persistent hyperplasis are inherited independently and the inheritance is complex in the F2 progeny of the F1 hybrids.
the susceptibility to phototumor induction and persistent hyperplastic response in the SENCAR mouse are controlled by a single recessive gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown that susceptibility to phototumorigenesis is not completely recessive to C57BL/10 and BALB/c genotypes, and that the degree of susceptibility is inversely proportional to the degree of hyperplasia.

the genetic factors that contribute to persistent epidermal cell hyperproliferation in response to UV radiation damage are the same factors that contribute to susceptibility to UV radiation-induced skin tumors in mice.
the F1 offspring from the reciprocal F1 crosses between SENCAR, BALB/c and C57BL6 mice are all resistant to phototumor formation and persistent epidermis hyperplasia.
